## Core Overview
- Course Code: CSC301 - Design and Analysis of Algorithms
- Primary Purpose: To build core competencies in designing, analyzing, and proving the correctness of efficient algorithms.
- Fundamental Themes: Algorithmic paradigms (Brute Force, Divide and Conquer, Decrease and Conquer, Transform and Conquer, Dynamic Programming, Greedy), time and space complexity analysis, and computational complexity (P, NP, NP-complete).

## Key Concepts & Theorems/Formulas
- Asymptotic Notations: Big-O, Big-Omega, and Big-Theta for defining worst-case, best-case, and average-case behaviors.
- Recurrence Relations: Methods for solving recurrences including Substitution Method, Recurrence Tree Method, and the Master Method (T(n) = aT(n/b) + f(n)).
- Algorithmic Techniques:
  - Brute Force & Decrease and Conquer (constant factor reduction, topological sorting).
  - Divide and Conquer (Closest-Pair, Convex-Hull, Matrix Multiplication).
  - Dynamic Programming (Edit Distance, LCS, Knapsack, Matrix Chain Multiplication).
  - Greedy Approach (Data Compression, Coin Change).
- Correctness Proofs: Pre-conditions, post-conditions, loop invariants, and mathematical induction for iterative and recursive algorithms.
- Complexity Classes: Definitions and examples of P, NP, and NP-complete problems.

## Exam Takeaways
- High-Yield Topics: Solving recurrence relations using the Master Method and designing algorithms via Dynamic Programming and Divide and Conquer.
- Critical Definitions: Loop invariants, asymptotic bounds, and the distinction between P and NP-complete classes.
- Assessment Focus: Expect analytical problem-solving questions on algorithm efficiency (CLO-4) and practical algorithmic design tasks (CLO-2).
